name: UTM Builder
title: UTM Builder: Free Campaign URL Generator for GA4
description: Build clean UTM links for email, social and ads. Adds utm_source, utm_medium and utm_campaign, keeps them lowercase, and warns about mistakes. Runs in your browser.
card: Tag campaign links with clean, consistent UTM parameters.
lede: Paste a page URL, fill in source, medium and campaign, and copy a tagged link that GA4 and HubSpot can attribute.
answer_q: How do I build a UTM link?
answer: Add `utm_source`, `utm_medium` and `utm_campaign` to the end of your page URL as query parameters, all in lowercase. This tool does it for you: fill in the fields and copy the result.
steps: Paste the landing page URL into Website URL.
Enter where the click comes from in Campaign source, for example `linkedin` or `newsletter`.
Enter the type of traffic in Campaign medium, for example `email`, `social` or `cpc`.
Name the campaign, then add term or content only if you need to split results further.
Copy the tagged URL and use it in your post, email or ad.

examples.title: LinkedIn post for a product launch
examples.input:
URL: https://example.com/pricing
Source: linkedin
Medium: social
Campaign: spring launch

examples.title: Two buttons in one email
examples.text: Use utm_content to tell links in the same email apart, for example `hero-button` and `footer-link`. Source, medium and campaign stay the same so the email reports as one campaign.

faq.a: GA4 needs `utm_source` and `utm_medium` to place a visit in a channel. `utm_campaign` is strongly recommended. `utm_term`, `utm_content` and `utm_id` are optional.
Yes. Analytics tools treat `Email` and `email` as different values, so mixed case splits your reports. The tool lowercases by default.

faq.q: Can I put UTM links on my own website?
faq.a: No. Tagging internal links starts a new session and overwrites the original source, so a visitor from Google can end up credited to your own banner. Use UTMs only on links from outside your site.
Yes. HubSpot reads the same UTM parameters on page views and form submissions, and its own tracking URL builder produces the same format.

faq.q: What happens if the URL already has a query string or #anchor?
faq.a: The tool keeps existing parameters and the anchor, and replaces only UTM parameters you fill in.
